title: Xenon Night: A PWR Core, Neutron by Neutron
subject: A full 3411 MWt pressurized-water reactor core is simulated live: two-group neutron diffusion on 18,496 cells, iodine-xenon poisoning, fuel and moderator temperature feedback, and automatic rods and boron. It runs through a night of grid load-follow and a dropped control rod, and a 6-worker Monte Carlo neutron transport run checks the eigenvalue independently.
why_hard: Three coupled timescales in one screen: neutron generations (microseconds, in the Monte Carlo), point kinetics after each rod step (seconds, inhour equation) and xenon poisoning (hours), all driven by one eigenvalue solver. That solver has to be correct, not just plausible: at boot it is checked against the published IAEA 2D PWR benchmark (k_eff = 1.02959). On top of that: a hand-written red-black SOR power iteration on a 136×136 two-group mesh with harmonic-mean coupling and vacuum boundaries; per-cell exact-exponential I/Xe integration; calibrated Doppler and moderator feedback; a quasi-static rod and boron controller; delta-tracking Monte Carlo spread over 6 Web Workers with Shannon-entropy source convergence. Then a 60 fps dark cockpit with a 17×17 assembly map carrying two tiny numbers per assembly, neutron tracks drawn over it, 4 field maps and 12 live charts, with no libraries.
angle: Opus 5.5 at maximum effort, no libraries, one night: hand-written WebGL for the field heatmaps, canvas 2D for everything else, a diffusion Web Worker plus 6 Monte Carlo Web Workers, Float64Array numerics
science:
CORE MODEL: the IAEA 2D PWR benchmark (ANL-7416 Supplement 2, Problem 11), mirrored to a full core so asymmetric tilts can develop. 17×17 assemblies at a 20 cm pitch (340 cm across). Transcribe the published quarter-core region map exactly: it is diagonally symmetric, and the 'fuel 2 + rod' assemblies sit at quarter positions (1,1), (1,5), (5,1), (5,5), giving 9 rodded assemblies in the full core, which become Bank D. Corners outside the staircase boundary are void. Mesh: 2.5 cm (8×8 cells per assembly), 136×136 = 18,496 cells.
Two-group constants [D1, D2, Σ1→2, Σa1, Σa2, νΣf2] (cm, cm⁻¹; νΣf1 = 0, χ1 = 1): Fuel1 = 1.5, 0.4, 0.02, 0.01, 0.080, 0.135. Fuel2 = 1.5, 0.4, 0.02, 0.01, 0.085, 0.135. Fuel2+rod = 1.5, 0.4, 0.02, 0.01, 0.130, 0.135. Reflector = 2.0, 0.3, 0.04, 0.0, 0.010, 0. Axial buckling B² = 0.8e-4 cm⁻² in both groups.
Equations: −∇·D1∇φ1 + (Σa1 + Σ12 + D1B²)φ1 = (1/k)·νΣf2·φ2 and −∇·D2∇φ2 + (Σa2 + D2B²)φ2 = Σ12·φ1. 5-point mesh-centred finite differences. Interior face coupling = 2·Di·Dj/(Di + Dj)/h². Outer boundary from the benchmark condition −D·∂φ/∂n = 0.4692·φ, so the boundary-face leakage term is 1/(h·(h/(2D) + 1/0.4692)).
Solver: power iteration with source S = νΣf2·φ2 and k ← k·ΣS_new/ΣS_old. Inner solve per group by red-black SOR (ω = 1.60 by default, 3 sweeps per group per outer). Converged when |Δk| < 1e-6 and max|ΔS|/S < 1e-5. Each solve is warm-started from the previous flux. Dominance ratio estimate = ‖S_n − S_{n−1}‖ / ‖S_{n−1} − S_{n−2}‖. Residual and k are kept for every outer iteration.
BOOT VALIDATION: solve the clean benchmark (all 9 rods in, no xenon, no boron, no feedback). The result must land within about ±30 pcm of the reference 1.02959. Display it and log it: 'IAEA-2D k = 1.0296x, ref 1.02959, Δ = n pcm'.
OPERATING STATE: Bank D insertion f = (228 − steps)/228 blends the 9 rodded assemblies: Σa2 = 0.085 + f·(0.130 − 0.085).
Boron: Σa2 += 6.8e-6·ppm in fuel cells. The measured worth (about −8 pcm/ppm) is shown.
Xenon: Σa2 += σX·X with σX = 2.65e-18 cm².
Feedback per cell, from relative power density q:
- Tm = 565 K + 18 K·P_core_frac.
- Tf = Tm + 600 K·q.
- Doppler: Σa1 = 0.010·[1 + aD·(√Tf − √Tf_ref)].
- Moderator: Σa2 += aM·(Tm − Tm_ref).
Calibrate aD and aM so the core Doppler coefficient is about −2.5 pcm/K and the total power defect from 0 to 100% is about −1600 pcm. Measure both with the solver and display the measured values.
Power normalisation: P = H·Σ_cells κ·Σf2·φ2·h², with Σf2 = νΣf2/2.43, κ = 3.204e-11 J, H = 366 cm, P_rated = 3411 MWt. This gives the absolute flux used for xenon burnout.
I-135/Xe-135, per cell, with F = Σf2·φ2:
- dI/dt = γI·F − λI·I
- dX/dt = γX·F + λI·I − (λX + σX·φ2)·X
Constants: γI = 0.0639, γX = 0.00237, λI = 2.87e-5 s⁻¹, λX = 2.09e-5 s⁻¹. Integrate exactly (analytic exponentials, φ held constant) over each 5-minute macro step. Xenon worth: every 30 sim-minutes run one extra warm-started solve with X = 0, then ρXe = (1/k_noXe − 1/k)·1e5 pcm. At equilibrium full power this comes out near −2800 to −3000 pcm.
CONTROL (quasi-static): power follows the demand schedule, which the automatic controller holds. Each macro step, compute the solve and ρ = (k − 1)/k. If |ρ| > 10 pcm, move Bank D by n = ρ/(differential worth) steps; the worth is a finite difference from the last move. Boron dilutes or borates at no more than the dilution limit (ppm/min) to drive Bank D back toward 210 steps.
Schedule: daily load-follow at 1%/min, 100% → 50% at 20:00 and back to 100% at 02:00. Dropped rod: at Day 3 23:00 the SW diagonal Bank D rod (assembly column 4, row 12, 0-based from top-left) falls fully in and stays in.
POINT KINETICS for each rod step: 6-group Keepin U-235 data, βi = [0.000215, 0.001424, 0.001274, 0.002568, 0.000748, 0.000273] (β = 0.0065), λi = [0.0124, 0.0305, 0.111, 0.301, 1.14, 3.01] s⁻¹, Λ = 2.0e-5 s. Take the residual reactivity ρ of the step.
- Solve the inhour equation ρ = ωΛ + Σ βi·ω/(ω + λi) for the dominant root by bisection. Stable period T = 1/ω.
- Prompt jump = β/(β − ρ).
- Integrate the 7 ODEs with backward Euler (dt = 1 ms) over 0–120 s for the response trace.
Precursor concentrations Ci are integrated over the real power history.
INDICES:
- QPTR = max quadrant power / mean quadrant power. Quadrants split on the core axes; centre-line cells count half to each side. Tech-spec warning at 1.02.
- F_xy = max assembly power / mean fuel-assembly power.
- F_cell = max cell power / mean cell power.
- Assembly power is shown to 3 decimals, with its change versus 1 sim-hour ago.
MONTE CARLO cross-check: 2D transport on the same mesh and a material snapshot (rods, boron, Xe, feedback), refreshed every 2 sim-hours.
- Σt,g = 1/(3·D_g).
- At each collision: absorption probability (Σa_g + D_g·B²)/Σt (buckling leakage treated as absorption); downscatter probability Σ12/Σt in group 1; otherwise isotropic scattering. Directions are sampled in 3D and the flight is projected onto x-y (dxy = s·sinθ).
- Woodcock delta-tracking with a mesh majorant. Neutrons crossing the outer boundary are lost.
- Collision estimator k_gen = Σ w·νΣf2/Σt / N. Fission sites are banked and resampled to N per generation.
- Shannon entropy over a 17×17 assembly-binned source: H = −Σ p·log2 p.
- 50 inactive generations, then active mean k_MC ± σ (σ = std/√n). Show Δ(MC − diffusion) in pcm, which is expected to be within a few hundred pcm because it is transport versus diffusion.
- 20,000 neutrons per generation split over 6 workers. Report histories/s and the running total. The last ~300 histories are kept as polylines for drawing (fast group violet-white, thermal group Cherenkov blue).

design.layout: A night-shift reactor-physics cockpit on the 1920×1080 stage, 8 px margins and gutters, three columns. Left rail (352 px): operator controls, the rod-step kinetics instrument and the event log, like a control-room operator desk. Centre hero (760×760): the full 17×17 core map, the subject itself, with a 680 px heatmap at 2.5 cm resolution, assembly grid lines, two tiny numbers in every assembly, Bank D rod markers, Monte Carlo neutron tracks over the top, and x/y flux-profile traces along the two outer edges. Below the hero, two strips show how the numbers are made: the diffusion solver's convergence and the Monte Carlo tallies. Right column (776 px): the time story as stacked strip charts sharing one 48 h sim-time axis (xenon/iodine, load-follow and control, tilt and peaking), then 4 small-multiple field maps, then the PC resources drawn as a 'compute plant' panel in the same instrument language (16 CPU threads as rod-position-indicator columns). The core sits at the centre because everything else is derived from it: the left side acts on it, the right side records its history.

design.fonts: Bahnschrift (semi-condensed) for panel titles, status chips and labels, styled like control-room mimic boards; Cascadia Mono for every number, axis tick, log line and per-assembly value (9–11 px); Segoe UI Variable Small for the tiny unit captions
design.feel: A PWR control room at 3 a.m. crossed with core-physics code output and the Cherenkov blue of a spent-fuel pool. Near-black navy panels with hairline grid rules. Power heatmap ramp: deep navy → Cherenkov blue → cyan → white → amber → red. Iodine in violet, xenon in amber. Rod positions drawn like DRPI columns. Calm and dense, with the slow menace of xenon building while everything ticks.

mid_work:
When the first frame is recorded it is Day 3 about 19:30 sim time, 30 minutes before the evening ramp-down. Every 48 h chart already holds two full days of load-follow cycles (two xenon dips and two xenon pits with their peak markers). Bank D and boron traces show the controller's history. The log is full: the boot benchmark line, hundreds of rod moves and boron dilutions, solver lines and MC summaries. The Monte Carlo is several hundred generations into its active cycles with a tight σ band and a flat Shannon entropy. The kinetics panel shows the latest rod step, and the compute plant has 35 s of thread history.
How: at page load the diffusion worker does four things in under 3 s. (1) It solves the clean IAEA benchmark and logs the validation. (2) It switches to the operating state and iterates equilibrium xenon at 100% with a critical boron search. (3) It fast-forwards with 15-minute macro steps from Day 1 00:00 to Day 3 10:45, through both earlier load-follow nights, filling every history buffer and the log. (4) It hands off to real time at 15 sim-min/s. The 6 MC workers start immediately. Then the recorder's 35 s warm-up carries the clock to about 19:30.
During the video (about 13 sim-hours), all of these happen on camera: the ramp to 50% at 20:00, xenon building, the SW rod drop at 23:00 (red flash, QPTR climbing past 1.02, the core map visibly tilting while the camera is on that quadrant), the 02:00 ramp back up into a deep xenon pit with Bank D withdrawing, and xenon peaking near 03:00–05:00.

post_angle: Day 3 of pushing Claude to the edge. Opus built a nuclear reactor core simulator overnight with no libraries. A 3411 MW PWR is solved as two-group neutron diffusion on 18,496 cells. It reproduces the IAEA benchmark to within {keff_benchmark} and runs a night of grid load-follow. Xenon-135 sinks the core into a {xenon_peak_pcm} pcm pit, a control rod drops and tilts the power to QPTR {qptr_max}, and {neutrons_tracked} Monte Carlo neutrons across 6 threads check the answer independently: k = {keff_mc}. Every number on screen comes from the physics.
